corrected_draft.description_long: On August 21, 2026, U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas of the Southern District of New York ruled in Catholic Legal Immigration Network v. Rubio that the State Department’s policy suspending immigrant-visa issuance to nationals of 75 countries was contrary to law and exceeded Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s authority. The court vacated the policy under the Administrative Procedure Act and set aside refusals of immigrant visas based solely on the policy, remanding those applications to consular officers for further adjudication. It expressly did not disturb visa refusals based on other statutory grounds, even when officials also cited the policy. Reuters reported the ruling on August 21 U.S. time and published its account the following day; the full court opinion is the primary support for the date, legal holding, and remedy. The policy had been announced in January 2026 and took effect on January 21, but the event here is the August ruling, not the earlier suspension. The record does not establish the outcome for every individual applicant after remand, later appeals, or immediate administrative compliance. It should not imply that all affected visas were issued or that every immigration restriction was invalidated.

remaining_gap: The accessed opinion establishes the ruling and remedy, but not subsequent appellate action, implementation, or individual visa outcomes after remand.

corrected_draft.description_long: On September 2, 2026, U.S. District Judge Beryl A. Howell granted California’s motion for a preliminary injunction in California v. EPA (D.D.C. No. 26-cv-2185). It required EPA to restore the status quo that existed before that release, withdraw or correct public reclassification statements, and refrain from giving effect to the reclassification while the injunction remains in place. The order set a September 21 deadline for a compliance status report and remains effective until further order. It also denied EPA’s motion to dismiss and the motions filed by industry intervenors. Reuters described the ruling as blocking EPA’s effort to send California’s rules to Congress for potential repeal; the primary injunction states its operative terms as above. This is preliminary relief in ongoing litigation, not a final merits judgment resolving all disputes over California’s emissions standards or waivers. It is distinct from California’s original waiver grants and earlier federal litigation over other programs.

child_drafts.title: Israel launches strikes against Iran
child_drafts.description_short: Israel launched strikes against Iran on June 13, 2025; Iran retaliated with missile attacks, Reuters reported.
child_drafts.description_medium: Reuters reported that Israel began strikes on Iran on June 13, 2025, targeting nuclear and military sites amid tensions over Iran’s nuclear program. Iran retaliated with missile attacks that night, with explosions reported in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv. This Israeli campaign preceded the separate U.S. strikes on Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan on June 21–22.
child_drafts.description_long: Israel began strikes against Iran on June 13, 2025, targeting nuclear and military infrastructure amid tensions over Iran’s nuclear program. Reuters reported that Iran retaliated that night with missile salvos, with explosions heard in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv. Israel’s military said fewer than 100 missiles had been fired and that most were intercepted or fell short; U.S. forces helped shoot down some missiles headed toward Israel, according to U.S. officials. The International Atomic Energy Agency chief told the U.N. Security Council that the above-ground pilot enrichment plant at Natanz had been destroyed, while damage at other sites remained under assessment. Iran’s U.N. envoy said 78 people were killed and more than 320 wounded in Israel’s strikes, most of them civilians. Israeli officials said the operation would continue.
child_drafts.draft_limitation: Draft contains only facts directly supported by the cited sources.

child_drafts.title: United States strikes Iranian nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan
child_drafts.description_short: U.S. forces struck Iran’s Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan nuclear sites on June 21–22, 2025, Reuters reported.
child_drafts.description_medium: Reuters reported that U.S. forces used B-2 bombers and other weapons in strikes on three Iranian nuclear sites. Iranian officials confirmed an attack on Fordow. The extent of damage remained uncertain in contemporaneous reporting, so claims that the sites were wholly destroyed require qualification.
child_drafts.description_long: U.S. forces struck the Iranian nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan during the night of June 21 into June 22, 2025. Reuters reported that B-2 bombers and other U.S. weapons were used, including six bunker-buster bombs against Fordow and 30 Tomahawk missiles at Natanz and Isfahan. Iranian officials confirmed an attack on Fordow. President Trump described the sites as obliterated, but contemporaneous damage assessments remained uncertain. The operation followed Israel’s June 13 campaign and was conducted by U.S. forces as a separate action. The strikes came after Iran ruled out another round of nuclear talks at that stage. Reuters reported that the United States also used diplomatic channels with Tehran on the day of the attack.
